title: design contents
description: The whole design as read, from describe design: every document grouped by kind, the files that could not be read, the board section as taken, the focus, the purpose and how the design is kept, so a reader can draw the design from one answer.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/designer/app/v1: the form of e-designer's answers. An app's answers keep the family app (apiversion/v1/forms.yaml), apart from the files they describe.

kind.description: Always DesignContents, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

ran.description: Where the answer came from; this contract fixes the app and the contract version, so an answer from anything else fails here.

app.description: Always designer, e-designer's product ID, since only e-designer gives this answer.

contract.description: Always v1, the contract version this schema belongs to.

data.description: The design's documents and what e-designer read from them.

kinds.description: Every kind the design holds, with its documents, design.yml, definitions.yml and layout.yml included.

additionalProperties.description: The kind's documents, in id order.

path.description: The file it is in, relative to the design.

changedAt.description: The file's last change, in Unix milliseconds, 0 when it could not be read, so a reader can tell what changed since it last looked.

document.description: The document as its file holds it: a resource, or for the kind Layout, layout.yml.

oneOf.description: layout.yml as read: where the boxes and lines of each view sit. Its version says its form; a version 1 file is refused by the board, which says to run e-designer migrate layout.

version.description: The form of layout.yml, so a reader knows how to read views.

views.description: Each view's boxes, lines and hexagon, keyed by view name, as apply --help describes them; the board writes them, so their inner shape is the layout program's.

broken.description: Every file e-designer could not read, and why, so a reader shows it instead of drawing a design with a hole in it (G-CODE-6).

file.description: The file, relative to the design.

message.description: Why it could not be read, for people.

board.description: design.yml's spec.board as the board takes it.

section.description: The section with every entry e-designer refuses left out. Written by the design's user, so it stays open.

problems.description: Every entry left out, and why.

focus.description: What the design is focused on now, the blocks and groups marked with a star.

order.description: Its place in the focus, counted from 1, as the board numbers the stars.

title.description: Its title, empty when it has none.

note.description: Why the design is focused so, in the user's words; absent when nothing is said.

since.description: Since when, as the user wrote it; absent when nothing is said.

problems.description: Every focus entry that names nothing the design holds.

purpose.description: What the design counts as, read as get design reads it; null when design.yml cannot be read.

oneOf.description: design.yml cannot be read, so the purpose is not known.

purpose.description: The word of the purpose list.

set.description: True when design.yml states it; false when it is the default.

label.description: How get design names it, such as reference (not set).

storage.description: How the design is kept: distributed, one file per resource, or single, one file (design storage).

problem.description: One thing e-designer could not take, with where it is, so nobody has to hunt for it.

at.description: Where the problem is: a file and a path in it, such as spec.board.display.layout.

says.description: What is wrong, in words for people; a program never decides by it (G-STACK-15).

document.description: One resource as its file holds it, in the form this contract reads.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/designer/design/v2, the form a design's files are written in at this contract (apiversion/v1/forms.yaml).

kind.description: The resource's kind, a built-in kind or one the design declares.

metadata.description: What names the resource, apart from what it says.

id.description: The resource's id, unique within its kind; other resources point to it by it.

title.description: The resource's name for people, shown on its card on the board.

tags.description: Labels the design's user puts on the resource.

spec.description: What the resource says. Written by the design's user, so it stays open: a design's fields are its own (CT-RULE-4).
